general.q: Which European capital city is built across a total of 14 islands?
general.why: The Swedish capital is connected by 57 bridges across its many islands.

general.q: Which bird has the largest wingspan of any living species, measuring up to 3.5 metres?
general.why: These massive seabirds can spend years at sea without touching land.

general.q: Who was the last English king to die in battle, falling at the Battle of Bosworth Field in 1485?
general.why: His remains were famously discovered under a car park in Leicester in 2012.

general.q: What is the predominant flavour of the French liqueur Cointreau?
general.why: It is a clear, orange-flavoured triple sec produced in Saint-Barthélemy-d'Anjou.

general.q: The English word 'shampoo' originated from a word in which language?
general.why: The word 'champo' originally meant to press, knead, or massage the muscles.

pop.q: In the sci-fi sitcom Red Dwarf, what is the full name of the holographic character played by Chris Barrie?
pop.why: Arnold J. Rimmer is the self-important, neurotic technician who is the only crew member Dave Lister can't stand.

pop.q: What is the real name of Sonic the Hedgehog's two-tailed fox sidekick, known as Tails?
pop.why: His name is a pun on 'miles per hour', fitting the high-speed theme of the Sega game series.

pop.q: In a classic 1983 Yellow Pages advert, an elderly man searches for a copy of which fictional book?
pop.why: The advert was so popular that a real book titled Fly Fishing by J.R. Hartley was published in 1991.

pop.q: In the 1985 cult classic film The Goonies, what is the name of the pirate whose treasure the kids are hunting for?
pop.why: One-Eyed Willy's booby-trapped ship, the Inferno, is hidden in a cavern beneath Astoria, Oregon.

pop.q: In the comedy series The Fast Show, which character is known for the catchphrase "I was very, very drunk"?
pop.why: Rowley Birkin QC usually tells long, mumbling stories that end with him admitting his intoxication.

music.q: Which 1980s band took their name from a villain in the 1968 science fiction film 'Barbarella'?
music.why: The character Dr. Durand Durand was a mad scientist in the cult film starring Jane Fonda.

music.q: Which 1991 Nirvana album is often credited with bringing alternative rock into the mainstream?
music.why: Featuring 'Smells Like Teen Spirit', it famously knocked Michael Jackson off the top of the US album charts.

music.q: After Peter Gabriel's departure in 1975, which member of Genesis took over as the band's lead singer?
music.why: Collins was the band's drummer before stepping up to the microphone for the album 'A Trick of the Tail'.

music.q: Which song's music video was the first ever to be broadcast on MTV in the United States in August 1981?
music.why: Performed by The Buggles, the song's title was a cheeky nod to the launch of the music television channel.

music.q: What was the title of Oasis's record-breaking debut studio album, released in August 1994?
music.why: It became the fastest-selling debut album in UK history at the time, featuring the hit 'Live Forever'.

mix.q: Which English band released the 1995 album 'Different Class', featuring the hit single 'Common People'?
mix.why: Jarvis Cocker's band helped define the Britpop era with this Mercury Prize-winning album.

mix.q: Which European city is famous for its historic Spanish Riding School and the Lipizzaner horses?
mix.why: Vienna has hosted the school for over 450 years, despite the 'Spanish' name of the horses.

mix.q: In the BBC sitcom 'Blackadder Goes Forth', what is the name of the dim-witted lieutenant played by Hugh Laurie?
mix.why: Hugh Laurie played Lieutenant George, while Tim McInnerny previously played the role of Lord Percy.

mix.q: Which 1985 Kate Bush album reached number one in the UK, knocking Madonna's 'Like a Virgin' off the top spot?
mix.why: It was her first number one album since her debut and was recorded in her own purpose-built studio.

mix.q: Which of Henry VIII’s wives was the mother of Queen Elizabeth I?
mix.why: Elizabeth was the only child of Henry and Anne Boleyn to survive infancy.

mix.q: In the 1993 film 'Jurassic Park', what species of dinosaur is the first one seen by the visitors?
mix.why: The sight of the towering Brachiosaurus remains one of cinema's most iconic and groundbreaking moments.

mix.q: Which noble gas, with the symbol Ne, is known for its bright reddish-orange glow in vacuum discharge tubes?
mix.why: Discovered in 1898, neon is widely used across the world in high-voltage advertising signs.

mix.q: Which 2006 album by Amy Winehouse features the hits 'Rehab' and 'You Know I'm No Good'?
mix.why: Produced by Mark Ronson and Salaam Remi, it won five Grammy Awards in a single night.

mix.q: Which British cheese is traditionally produced in the counties of Derbyshire, Leicestershire, and Nottinghamshire?
mix.why: Blue Stilton has a Protected Designation of Origin status and cannot be made in the village of Stilton itself.

mix.q: On which Nintendo console did 'The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time' first appear in 1998?
mix.why: Often cited as one of the greatest games ever, it was a landmark 3D title for the N64.
